claims.text: Motivation is the willingness of an employee to work hard towards the business's goals because the work, the rewards or the surroundings give the worker a reason to do so.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: People work for money - wages and salaries pay for the needs and wants of a household - and also for non-money reasons: satisfaction from doing a job well, the company of workmates, the status a role carries and a sense of achievement.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: Where pay is too low to live on, money dominates the reasons people work; once pay covers the basics, the non-money reasons grow in importance.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: Different workers respond to different rewards, so a manager benefits from understanding why each worker works before choosing a method of motivation.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: Labour productivity is the output each worker produces in a given period, such as crates per packer per day.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: Absenteeism is the rate at which employees are absent from work when they are expected to be present, usually measured in days lost per worker per period.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: Labour turnover is the rate at which employees leave a business and have to be replaced, usually expressed as a percentage of the workforce per year.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: A well-motivated workforce tends to show higher labour productivity, lower absenteeism and lower labour turnover, because motivated workers care about the outcome of their work; the benefit compounds through lower unit costs and less spending on replacing leavers.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: Maslow's hierarchy arranges human needs in levels, and a lower level generally has to be reasonably satisfied before the next level up motivates behaviour.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: The levels of Maslow's hierarchy are physiological needs, safety needs, social needs, esteem needs and self-actualisation; pay and safe conditions serve the lower levels, while recognition, responsibility and growth serve the upper ones.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: A satisfied need no longer motivates, so a manager who diagnoses the lowest unsatisfied level can aim rewards where they are likely to move the worker, and avoid spending where they will not.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: Taylor held that workers are motivated mainly by money: he recommended dividing work into simple repeated tasks, teaching the one fastest method, and linking pay to output so more effort earns more.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: Taylor's approach tends to raise output where low pay is the binding problem, but it ignores boredom and the higher needs, and piece-rate pay can reward speed at the cost of quality.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: Herzberg distinguished hygiene factors - pay, working conditions, job security - whose weakness causes dissatisfaction, from motivators - achievement, recognition, responsibility, growth - which create motivation.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: Improving hygiene factors alone tends to remove dissatisfaction without creating effort, because motivation comes from motivators; a business whose jobs offer none cannot fix low motivation with pay alone.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: The main financial rewards are wages, salaries, bonuses, commission and profit sharing.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: A wage is pay by the hour or day for time worked; a salary is a fixed sum per month or year; a bonus is an extra payment for reaching a target; commission is a share of the value of each sale; profit sharing gives workers a stated share of the business's profits.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: Financial rewards meet money needs directly, but their motivational effect tends to fade once the payment is accepted as normal, and their cost recurs - so money is a strong lever where pay is genuinely inadequate and a weak one where it is not.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: The main non-financial methods of motivation are job enrichment, job rotation, teamworking, training and opportunities for promotion.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: Job enrichment redesigns a job to add responsibility, challenge and variety; job rotation moves a worker between different tasks on a schedule; teamworking organises a group around a shared goal with shared responsibility; training raises skills; and opportunities for promotion open a path to a better role.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: Non-financial methods aim at the upper levels of human needs - esteem and self-actualisation - so they can motivate where pay cannot, but they take time and management effort, and they rarely help workers whose basic pay is inadequate.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: Recommending a method of motivation depends on diagnosing the actual cause of the low motivation, on the needs of the particular workers, and on what the business can afford; a method that does not reach the named cause is likely to fail.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: A working pattern for recommendations: where pay is too low, financial reward comes first; where pay is adequate but the work is monotonous, rotation and enrichment fit; where workers see no future, training and a visible promotion path fit.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.
